children: with an overweight rating, saying that the precision oncology therapy developer's pipeline of RAS(“ON”) inhibitors will lead to long-term success.
The investment bank has a price target of $255 (~23% upside based on Sept. 9 close).

Analyst Sean Laaman said that RAS mutations are seen in ~30% of all cancers and "represent an addressable pool of ~100,000 patients annually in key solid tumors today, including pancreatic, lung, and colorectal cancer."
Revolution received a major boost in late August with the US FDA
of its first-in-class targeted pancreatic cancer treatment Rasonque (daraxonrasib).

Laaman noted that the approval "positions the company to capture a significant share of what could become a multi-billion-dollar oncology market with ~$12bn of modeled peak risk-adjusted sales (~$18bn unadjusted) across the portfolio by 2036 (if all~100k addressable 'RAS patients' today across the core solid tumors were treated at Rasonque price, this implies a ~$40bn TAM)."

In the pipeline, he sees zoldonrasib as the next potential commercial opportunity given confirmed response rate and median progression-free survival data in non-small cell lung cancer. The candidate is also under investigation for pancreatic cancer and solid tumors.
Laaman also cited elironrasib as having potential upside in KRAS G12C cancers.
He added that "combination therapies represent a large source of long-term upside."

title: Revolution a new overweight at Morgan Stanley on RAS-targeted oncology franchise
